figure_162_cow.name: The sacred cow

descriptions.default: A cow wearing Hathor's crown, the sun disc between two plumes. Her spell puts warmth under the head of the dead, as she once did under the head of Ra, so the body stays warm as it was on earth.

figure_162_cow.reference: Davis 1894; Davis calls her only "the sacred cow": the name Ihet is not in his text

figure_163_eye_first.name: The winged eye

descriptions.default: An eye of Horus with wings and human legs. In its pupil stands a god with a bird-soul's face and the double plume, lifting his arm. Its spell keeps the body from decaying in the netherworld.

figure_163_eye_first.reference: Davis 1894; which pupil holds which god is my reading

descriptions.default: A snake walking on human legs, carrying the sun disc and horns. Its spell saves the dead from the one with a terrible face, whose mouth breathes fire to taste the souls.

figure_163_eye_second.name: The winged eye

descriptions.default: The second winged eye on legs. In its pupil stands a god with the face of Neith and the double plume, lifting his arm. With its spell the dead may go out and wander as they wish.

figure_163_eye_second.reference: Davis 1894; which pupil holds which god is my reading

figure_164_mut.name: Mut

descriptions.default: Mut with three heads, a lioness, a woman in the double crown and a falcon, and wide wings. She is the mother of the dead in their coffins: she saves their bones, and the worms shall not eat them.

figure_164_mut.reference: Davis 1894; the text also hails her as Sekhet-Bast-Ra

figure_164_dwarf_front.name: The dwarf

descriptions.default: A dwarf with two heads, a falcon's and a man's, the double plume on top, one arm raised. One stands before Mut and one behind her.

figure_164_dwarf_front.reference: Davis 1894; the vignette heading has a child's head where the rubric has a man's

descriptions.default: The second dwarf, the one behind Mut, with a falcon's head and a man's, the double plume and a raised arm.
A man with his arms at his sides and a ram's head on each shoulder. His image was drawn on the breast of the dead.

figure_165_amun.name: Amun, the Hidden

descriptions.default: A god with a scarab's body and the double plume, one arm raised. He is called by his secret names so that the body flourishes and the dead may rest whole in the netherworld. His image was placed on the heart.

figure_165_amun.reference: Davis 1894; the vignette heading names him Khem (Min), while the spell calls on Amun
